oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Unveiling the Untold: A Narrative Inquiry into the Experiences of an Asian American Woman Superintendent
oai_dc:dc.dc:creator: Resilla, Clare
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In this narrative inquiry, as a researcher, I examined how one Asian American woman in Texas made meaning of her leadership journey from her previous school and district leadership roles to her current role as deputy superintendent and her future aspiration to become a district superintendent. Drawing on Blackmore’s perspective on educational leadership and Irby et al.’ s synergistic leadership theory, I illuminated the underexplored experiences of an Asian woman seeking a position at the highest levels of K-12 educational leadership. I also investigated gatekeeping theory to analyze how existing selection processes for educational leadership influenced the participant’s career trajectories. By examining critical incidents such as career opportunities, barriers, and mentorships in a woman deputy superintendent’s narrative, I uncovered the vital roles of mentors and former supervisors as gatekeepers who shaped the participant’s leadership journey. Furthermore, I presented three overarching concepts, internal, external, and convergent, that contributed to the challenges and opportunities encountered on the pathway to the superintendent position.
